artists.biography:
Japan was an English music group formed in 1974 in Catford, South London. The band achieved success in the late 1970s and early 1980s, when they were often associated with the burgeoning New Romantic fashion movement (though the band denied any such connection).
Japan achieved nine UK Top 40 hits in the early 1980s, most notably "Ghosts" and their cover version of "I Second That Emotion", which were top ten hits in 1982. Their last ever performance was on 16 December 1982. The band suffered from personal and creative clashes and decided to split during a period when they were beginning to experience significant commercial success both in their native UK and internationally.
Japan have been cited as an important influence on 1980s synthpop bands such as Duran Duran and Camouflage.

perplexity.description:
Exorcising Ghosts is a 1984 compilation album by the British band Japan, released by Virgin Records. The album gathers key tracks from the group’s most influential period, spanning their early Hansa Records releases and their two seminal Virgin studio albums, Gentlemen Take Polaroids (1980) and Tin Drum (1981). Musically, the collection showcases Japan’s signature blend of electronic pop, art rock, and sophisticated production, marked by David Sylvian’s distinctive vocals, atmospheric textures, and the band’s fusion of Western pop with Eastern influences. The tracklist includes major singles such as “Gentlemen Take Polaroids,” “The Art of Parties,” “Visions of China,” “Quiet Life,” “Ghosts,” and “Nightporter,” as well as select rarities and live recordings.

As Japan’s definitive compilation, Exorcising Ghosts serves as both a career overview and an accessible entry point to the band’s legacy. Compiled in consultation with Sylvian after the group’s dissolution, it highlights their evolution from glam-tinged pop to a more refined, experimental sound. The album reached No. 45 on the UK Albums Chart and was later certified Gold by the BPI in 1997. Critics have noted its value as a starting point for new listeners, though some have observed that its focus on the Virgin era means it omits much of the band’s earlier, more rock-oriented material. Nonetheless, Exorcising Ghosts remains a crucial document of Japan’s impact on electronic and art pop in the early 1980s.
